title: Pollination & Seed Dispersal
keyIdea: Flowers make pollen on anthers; pollination moves pollen to a stigma so a seed can form; seeds then disperse (wind, animals, water, bursting) so new plants have space — not only so flowers look pretty.
familyTip: On a walk, find a flower and ask: where might pollen sit? Spot a dandelion clock or berry and ask how that seed might travel.

visual.caption: Life-cycle idea or mix-up? Drag each clue, or tap it then a box.

items: pollen moves from anther to stigma
after pollination a seed can form
flowers are only for looking pretty
seeds often travel away from the parent
pollination is the same as germination
wind, animals, water or burst disperse seeds

lab.caption: Flagship lab: dust anther pollen, move pollen to stigma, form a seed, pick a dispersal mode, catch decoration myth, order the life-cycle story.

kid: Pollen is made on the anthers of a flower.
Pollination means pollen lands on a stigma — often with help from insects or wind.
After that, a seed can form. Later the seed needs to travel away.
Seeds move by wind, animals, water, or a pod that bursts — so new plants have space.
adult: UK NC Y3 Plants: flowers in the life cycle — pollination, seed formation and seed dispersal. NGSS 2-LS2-2: a simple model of pollination or seed dispersal. Distinct from Growing from a seed (germination) and Parts of a Plant.

Words: anther, stigma, pollen, pollination, seed formation, dispersal. Common mistakes: flowers only for looks; mixing pollination with germination; seeds never leave the parent; pollen made in roots or leaves.
In the lab your child dusts anther pollen, moves it to the stigma, forms a seed, picks a dispersal mode, spots the decoration myth, and orders pollen → stigma → seed → disperse.

practice.hint: Look at the flower parts that hold dusty yellow grains.
practice.explain: Anthers make pollen. Roots and leaves have other jobs.
Pollination is pollen reaching a stigma. Sprouting is germination later.

choices: new plants have space away from the parent
practice.explain: Dispersal spreads offspring so they are less crowded.

practice.prompt: A bee visits {a} flowers and leaves pollen on each stigma. How many pollination events?
practice.hint: Count one pollination per stigma that receives pollen.
practice.explain: {a} stigma visits → {=a} pollination events in this simple count.

practice.prompt: {a} seeds blow away and {b} stick on the parent. How many dispersed?
practice.hint: Dispersed means they left the parent.

choices: Flowers are only for looking pretty
pool.explain: Flowers do pollination and seed work — not only decoration.

pool.hint: What must exist before a seed can travel?
pool.explain: Make pollen, pollinate, form a seed, then disperse.

choices: seeds that never leave the parent
pollen stuck forever on one anther
pool.hint: Think of light seeds like a dandelion clock blowing away.
pool.explain: Light seeds can ride the wind away from the parent.

choices: pollination moves pollen; germination is a seed starting to grow
pool.hint: Separate flower step from seedling step.
pool.explain: Pollination is pollen to stigma; germination is later growth from a seed.

pool.prompt: {a} anthers each dusted once. Pollen sources ready?
pool.hint: Count each anther that is dusted and ready.
pool.explain: {a} anthers ready → {=a} pollen sources in this count.

choices: seeds stuck to fur or eaten then dropped
seeds glued to the parent forever
pool.explain: Fur, beaks and droppings can carry seeds away.

pool.prompt: A stigma’s job in pollination is to…
pool.explain: The stigma receives pollen during pollination.

pool.hint: Add the ones that left and the ones that stayed.
